kill_argument: H1's confirmatory comparison is drawn finer than its instrument can resolve. The margin is 0.005 ECE, but plug-in 15-bin equal-mass ECE has a positive bias of about 0.01 at 5,000 test rows and 0.03 at 1,351 (design.threats[0]), and the bias is not additive: it sits at the floor for a well-calibrated model and shrinks toward zero as true miscalibration grows. If RF is the miscalibrated one, raw RF-minus-LR is pulled toward zero by up to LR's floor; if neither is, it equals the floor difference. ece_adj subtracts RF's full floor even where RF's bias is near zero, so the only check is biased against H1 by up to RF's floor. Neither metric separates a calibration difference of 0.005-0.03 from estimator artefact, and on phoneme the artefact is several margins wide. What held: preprocessing is train-only; the FrozenEstimator/ensemble=False path, binary predict_proba (1-p, no renormalisation), HGB's n_samples > 10_000 early-stopping switch and is_categorical_=None for arrays match the pinned sklearn 1.9.1 source; duplicate feature vectors are negligible; only data-prep runs exist; deferred question findings F6 and F13-F18 are addressed in plan.json.

findings.text: H1 margin (0.005 ECE) lies below the resolution of its estimator, and the pre-declared correction is biased in a known direction. Plug-in binned ECE per bin is E|g + e| with e of SD s = sqrt(p(1-p)/n_b): about 0.8 s when the true gap g is 0, about |g| when |g| >> s. With n_b = 333 (5,000 test rows) and p near 0.3, 0.8 s is about 0.02 per bin; with n_b = 90 (phoneme) about 0.04. So (i) raw RF-minus-LR is biased toward zero by up to LR's floor when RF is truly worse calibrated, and equals floor_RF - floor_LR when neither is; (ii) ece_adj = ece - ece_floor removes the whole floor from both models, which is right only for a calibrated model and over-corrects a miscalibrated one, so sensitivity (a) is biased against H1 by up to RF's floor. A disagreement between (a) and the confirmatory verdict, which step 11 promises to report, cannot then be read either way. sources/notes.md D1 pointed to the debiased estimator (kumar2019) or ECE_sweep (roelofs2022), both already verified in refs.bib; the design chose floor subtraction instead without saying why.

(2019) Def. G.3 debiased l1 ECE (M=1,000 normal draws), reported only (method steps 8 and 12a, threats[0]).

findings.text: sens-ncal equalises only calibration n. Phoneme also differs in training n (2,702 vs 10,000) and test n (1,351 vs 5,000), so a phoneme-specific H2 pattern that survives sens-ncal can still come from training size (a different base model) or test-set noise, not from the dataset. The stated purpose, 'separate the effect of calibration-set size from the dataset', is right only for calibration n.
findings.response: Designer: sens-ncal's purpose narrowed to equalising calibration n only; training n and test n differences on phoneme stated (method step 12b, analysis_plan, threats[2]).
